title: Islamic Umm al-Qura Calendar
intro: A tabulated Islamic lunar calendar associated with Saudi civil datekeeping. Here the implementation uses a maintained table of month starts for a bounded year range.
summary: Twelve lunar months; month starts are looked up in a predefined table, rather than extrapolated beyond it.
origin: The Umm al-Qura calendar is used in Saudi Arabian civil contexts. Its conventions are distinct from calculations that predict local crescent sightings.
structure: Dates use twelve Hijri months. Each month's length follows the stored table, typically 29 or 30 days.
pattern_note: This provider supports the maintained AH 1300–1600 table only. Other years must produce an unsupported-date result, not an invented extension.
history: Published Islamic month tables enable consistent scheduling and recordkeeping. Different Islamic authorities and local lunar sightings do not always select the same date.
example: A date in Ramadan AH 1447 can be interpreted using the stored table. Trying to display AH 1700 must be rejected instead of calculating an unsupported month.
limits: Historical sections of the table are retrospective. This provider does not establish official religious observance for all communities and does not cover years outside AH 1300–1600.
